arguments.summary: Latest filed data show strong reported profitability and operating cash generation for all four companies, but forward demand, supply, regulatory-risk detail and earnings-date evidence are not established in the seeded normalized facts. QQQ’s dated holdings show material, but stale, overlap with NVDA, MU and META; ANET is absent from the supplied table.

claims.text: ANET’s June 2026 10-Q reports six-month revenue of $5.745bn versus $4.210bn a year earlier, operating income of $2.536bn versus $1.845bn, net income of $2.236bn versus $1.703bn, and operating cash flow of $2.777bn versus $1.842bn. The filing reports $2.290bn cash plus $11.053bn marketable securities, against $8.922bn total liabilities at June 30.

MU’s May 2026 10-Q reports nine-month revenue of $78.959bn versus $26.063bn a year earlier, operating income of $55.589bn versus $6.116bn, and net income of $47.268bn versus $5.338bn. Its balance sheet reports $24.995bn cash, $5.722bn total debt (current plus long-term), and $100.724bn equity. The filing identifies AI-related demand, production ramps, new fabs, tariffs/trade regulations and government-incentive conditions as forward-looking risk channels.

META’s latest seeded filing facts, for the six months ended June 30, 2026, report $117.111bn revenue, $41.647bn operating income, $42.621bn net income, $64.088bn operating cash flow and $49.113bn capex. At period-end it reported $449.956bn assets, $188.735bn liabilities, $261.221bn equity, $15.462bn cash and $83.664bn long-term debt.

NVDA’s July 2026 10-Q reports six-month revenue of $177.837bn versus $90.805bn a year earlier, operating income of $117.270bn versus $50.078bn, net income of $118.010bn versus $45.197bn, and operating cash flow of $74.421bn versus $42.779bn. At July 26 it reported $22.443bn cash, $34.143bn marketable debt securities, $32.366bn long-term debt and $228.984bn equity; accounts receivable and inventories rose from $38.466bn and $21.403bn at January 25 to $63.059bn and $31.575bn, respectively.

QQQ’s sponsor holdings table dated September 12, 2026 lists NVDA at 8.45%, MU at 4.85% and META at 3.07%; the reported table coverage is 100.05% and top-10 weight is 47.17%. The table is marked stale (8 days old versus a 7-day maximum), and ANET is not listed in the supplied holdings table.

For 21/63-session scenario monitoring, reported earnings/cash strength provides capacity to absorb investment or working-capital needs, while MU’s explicitly disclosed supply, production-ramp, trade and incentive channels and NVDA’s higher receivables/inventory balances make demand realization and supply execution material variables. This is not a forecast.

gaps.description: No sourced forward guidance, consensus, next earnings dates, or detailed current demand/supply and regulatory-risk disclosures for ANET, META and NVDA were available in the seeded normalized facts/read excerpts; no valuation conclusion is supported.
QQQ holdings are stale and do not establish prospective weights; absence of ANET from the supplied table does not prove zero fund exposure.

arguments.counter_thesis: Historical profit and cash-flow growth may not persist if demand, supply execution, working-capital conversion, trade restrictions or regulation deteriorates; the available evidence does not quantify those forward changes.

review_conditions.description: Review next company filings/earnings releases for guidance, demand/supply, working-capital, capex and regulatory disclosures before relying on 21/63-session scenarios.

shared_exposures.mechanism: Dated QQQ look-through includes direct reported weights in NVDA, MU and META, so company-specific moves can transmit to QQQ; weights are stale and are not portfolio exposures.
shared_exposures.qualification: September 12 sponsor table is marked stale; ANET is not listed but missing-table inference is not permitted.
